Fix a finite list of named subsystems $s_1,\ldots,s_m$, where $m\in\mathbb N$ and $m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), each having its own equilibrium state domain $D_{c_i}$ as defined in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Their separated endpoint state space is the Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]])

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m}.$$

An **isolated compound** is the system consisting of those subsystems and any named auxiliaries or work devices included inside a declared outer boundary, with no matter or energy transfer across that outer boundary during the admitted process, in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. Transfers between constituents are internal to the compound. Its total energy and other extensive coordinates use the composition convention of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. The additive entropy sum applies only when the constituent split is admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems; an interacting compound outside that scope needs its own total-entropy model.

For specified totals and retained barriers, an **equilibrium feasible set** is the model-declared subset $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D$ of endpoint tuples satisfying those totals and exactly the exchange permissions in the declared protocol. Totals are imposed on the dimensioned coordinate maps $U_c,V_c,n_{c,j}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], not by treating the dimensionless numerical coordinates as quantities with units. For example, if two constituents are in thermal contact through [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]] while their volumes and mole amounts remain fixed, $\mathcal F$ consists of the energy partitions $(x_A,x_B)$ with the prescribed total energy and those fixed volumes and amounts. citations.quote: A record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$.
the adopted model balance is $$U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)=Q[P]+W_{\mathrm{on}}[P],$$
S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}
For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$, $$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$ Also $\log 1=0$.

For a system $s$ of constitution $c$, the process model fixes one Galilean inertial chart $g_s$ for kinetic-energy bookkeeping and transfer records and holds that chart fixed throughout each process. A process record is a tuple
$$P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P).$$
For each finite closed time interval $I_P=[t_0,t_1]\subseteq\mathbb R$ with $t_0<t_1$ as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, its component fields have these types: $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$ are equilibrium endpoint coordinates from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; $Z_s$ is the model-declared configuration space of the system, its auxiliaries and devices; $Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq Z_s$ is the model-declared set of equilibrium configurations and $\xi_s:Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_c$ assigns their state coordinates; $z_P:I_P\to Z_s$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]); $\mathcal K_s$ is the model-declared set of control/contact records and $\kappa_P\in\mathcal K_s$; and $\mathcal R_s$ is the model-declared set of signed transfer records and $r_P\in\mathcal R_s$. These fields form a finite Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]]). The admitted records $\mathcal P_s$ are the model-specified subset of tuples with these types that additionally satisfy $z_P(t_0),z_P(t_1)\in Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}$, $\xi_s(z_P(t_0))=x_P^-$, and $\xi_s(z_P(t_1))=x_P^+$. No continuity or differentiability is imposed on $z_P$, and its values at interior times need not represent equilibrium states.

For an endpoint bookkeeping quantity $F$, write $\Delta F=F_P^+-F_P^-$. A closed record in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] has no matter crossing the chosen outer boundary. The core closed-record class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\subseteq\mathcal P_s$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]) contains only records for which the system has a supplied total mass $M>0$ and defined center-of-mass velocities at both endpoints in the fixed chart $g_s$, so the kinetic energies $K_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm\|_2^2$ are defined as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. It further requires $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$, where $U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ denotes any model-specified external-field potential energy tracked separately from the internal-energy coordinate in $g_s$. Other process classes require an expanded energy bookkeeping rule.

For each $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$, the protocol supplies maps $Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}:\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\to\mathbb R$ whose values are interpreted in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]] and whose energy bookkeeping uses $g_s$. $Q[P]>0$ means energy enters the system through the declared thermal-transfer channel; $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]>0$ means mechanical work is done on the system. These are functionals of the process record, not state functions of $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$. Heat is the protocol-assigned thermal mode of energy transfer, not a quantity stored in the equilibrium state. A record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$. A closed record may still exchange energy; it is not thereby isolated.

A preparation is a model-specified rule selecting the particular initial equilibrium state $x_P^-$. A statistical extension may instead specify a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space, as in [[def-probability-measure]]; such a statistical preparation is outside this deterministic process class. A preparation does not assert later equilibration. An admitted record may pass through nonequilibrium configurations even though both endpoints lie in $D_c$.

derivations.claim: Put $\lambda:=p_f/p_i$. The equilibrium equations give $T_f/T_i=\lambda(9/10)$. The first-law balance gives $nC_V(T_f-T_i)=p_f(V_i-V_f)$, hence $(3/2)(\lambda(9/10)-1)=\lambda(1/10)$. Solving yields $\lambda=6/5$ and $T_f/T_i=27/25$.

The entropy difference is therefore $\Delta S=nR[(3/2)\ln(27/25)+\ln(9/10)]$. By [L1], $2\Delta S/(nR)=\ln\!\left((27/25)^3(9/10)^2\right)=\ln(1594323/1562500)>0$, since $1594323>1562500$ and $\log$ is strictly increasing with $\log 1=0$. Since $nR>0$, $\Delta S>0$.

derivations.claim: Each entropy in [A1] is finite, affine and continuous on the convex domain $(0,\infty)^3$, hence concave; it is $C^2$ with $S_{A,U}=2\,\mathrm{K^{-1}}$ and $S_{B,U}=1\,\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. Scaling every extensive coordinate by $\lambda$ scales each entropy by $\lambda$, and the admitted separated-system total is their sum. The pairs in [A1] are admitted by [F3], their fixed total energy uses the composition rule [F4], the separated entropy is the sum by [F5], and the tagged scaling is homogeneous by [F6]. Thus the model satisfies [F1]–[F6].

For each integer $n\ge2$, put $\mathcal U_n=\{\phi(x)\in\mathcal F:x<1-1/n\}$. It is relatively open: if $\phi(x)\in\mathcal U_n$, then $\epsilon=1-1/n-x>0$, and any $\phi(y)\in\mathcal F$ with $\|\phi(y)-\phi(x)\|_2<\epsilon$ has coordinate difference $\phi(y)-\phi(x)=(y-x,0,0,-(y-x),0,0)$. By [L3], $\|\phi(y)-\phi(x)\|_2=\sqrt2|y-x|$, so $|y-x|<\epsilon$ and $y<1-1/n$. Given any $x\in(0,1)$, [L1] applied to $1/(1-x)>1$ gives an integer $n>1/(1-x)$; then $n\ge2$ and $x<1-1/n$, so the $\mathcal U_n$ cover $\mathcal F$. For any nonempty finite subfamily with indices $n_1,\ldots,n_k$, [L2] gives a greatest index $N$, and its union is $\mathcal U_N$. The feasible state $\phi(1-1/(2N))$ belongs to $\mathcal F$ but not $\mathcal U_N$, so this cover has no finite subcover. By [A2] and [F7], $\mathcal F$ is noncompact and has no assumed attainment guarantee.
For every $x\in(0,1)$, the entropy value is $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x))=s_*(1+x)<2s_*$ because $s_*>0$. Thus $2s_*$ is an upper bound of the feasible entropy values.

Given any $\varepsilon>0$, apply [L1] to $2+s_*/\varepsilon$ to choose $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n>2+s_*/\varepsilon$. Then $x_n:=1-1/n\in(0,1)$ and $$0<2s_*-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x_n))=s_*/n<\varepsilon.$$ Hence feasible entropy values lie arbitrarily close to $2s_*$ from below.

Let $u$ be any upper bound of the feasible entropy values. If $u<2s_*$, set $d:=2s_*-u>0$ and apply [L1] to $2+s_*/d$ to choose $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n>2+s_*/d$. Then $x:=1-1/n\in(0,1)$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x))=2s_*-s_*/n>2s_*-d=u$, contradicting that $u$ is an upper bound. Therefore $2s_*\le u$ for every upper bound $u$. By [L4], $\sup\{S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x)):0<x<1\}=2s_*$.

For every $x\in(0,1)$, $y=(x+1)/2$ also lies in $(0,1)$ and satisfies $y>x$. Hence $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(y))=s_*(1+y)>s_*(1+x)=S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x))$ because $s_*>0$. No feasible state maximizes entropy; the supremum $2s_*$ is not attained because $x=1$ is excluded.
By [F8] stable equilibrium in this route requires an attained global maximum on the exact feasible set. Since no maximum is attained, this model has no stable equilibrium under that criterion.

citations.quote:
Adopt the following axioms for $\prec$ on every declared pair of finite compounds with equal formal mass in [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]. Initially this covers equal-composition adiabatic accessibility. If a later channel model admits comparisons between distinct composition types, the same axioms apply to those comparisons and all their finite scaled products; no cross-type transition is admitted by this postulate alone. They are assumptions of the operational model, not consequences of the process definition or of energy additivity.

**A1 (reflexivity).** $A\prec A$ for every state $A$.

**A2 (transitivity).** If $A\prec B$ and $B\prec C$, then $A\prec C$.

**A3 (consistency).** If $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every finite spectator compound $C$ for which both endpoint compounds are admitted and the resulting formal masses agree.

**A4 (scaling).** If $A\prec B$, then $\lambda A\prec\lambda B$ for every $\lambda>0$, using the tagged scaling maps of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]].

**A5 (splitting).** For each state $x$, positive $s<t$, and tagged scaled copies of its material, the state $t x$ is accessible in both directions to the separated pair $(s x,(t-s)x)$. This states reversible splitting of an equilibrium preparation into scaled copies, not additivity of arbitrary state functions.

**A6 (stability).** Let $A,B$ have equal formal mass. Let $Z_0,Z_1$ be fixed positive spectator compounds of equal formal mass, and let $\epsilon_n>0$ decrease to zero. If $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for every $n$, then $A\prec B$.

Equality of formal masses in A6 is required so each comparison is defined; equality of composition vectors is not required when a declared model includes cross-type transitions. A6 is a limiting closure assumption on the relation; it does not assert continuity of any physical process or the existence of a limiting apparatus.

For each simple-system chart $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$, $n_i\ge1$, let $x=(u,v)$, with one energy coordinate $u$ and $n_i$ work coordinates $v$. The chart is a nonempty open convex domain. The simple-compressible physical case is the fixed-composition slice and embedding of [[def-td-thermal-join]], with $n_i=1$, $u=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $v=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$. A declared multi-work chart or joined chart instead supplies its own equilibrium endpoint domain and diagonal unit map: $U=u(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $W_a=v_a w_a$ for fixed positive work-coordinate units $w_a$. The numerical domain is identified with these physical endpoints by that supplied map, and accessibility is pulled back from the admitted endpoint relation. These identifications preserve the internal-energy meaning and fixed composition; extra work coordinates do not follow from the simple-compressible state definition. Adopt these assumptions for every state $x$ and for every thermal join treated as a simple system:

**A7 (convex-combination accessibility).** For $0<t<1$, the separated scaled pair $(t x,(1-t)y)$ is accessible to the chart state $t x+(1-t)y$, whenever these states are in the declared domains.

For each $x$, define its forward sector $A_x=\{y\in\Gamma_i:x\prec y\}$. Adopt:

**S1 (strict successor).** Some $y\in\Gamma_i$ satisfies $x\prec\prec y$.

**S2 (unique finite-slope support).** At $x=(u_x,v_x)$, $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane through $x$, and it can be written
$$
u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0
$$
with finite $P_i(x)\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$. The map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$ is locally Lipschitz: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite Lipschitz constant bounds $\|P_i(x)-P_i(y)\|/\|x-y\|$. A supporting hyperplane means $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets it at $x$.

**S3 (connected relative boundary).** The boundary $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$, taken in the topology relative to $\Gamma_i$, is arcwise connected.

These are explicit adopted conditions. The slope $P_i$ is a geometric support parameter here; no equation identifying it with measured pressure is asserted. In particular, S1–S3 and A7 do not assert comparison hypothesis for products.

Use thermal joins and $\sim_T$ exactly as defined in [[def-td-thermal-join]]. For every ordered pair of simple systems and every admitted finite join, adopt:

**T1 (joining).** $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$.

**T2 (reversible splitting).** Every join state has at least one split into component states at its stated total energy and work coordinates that is reversible to the join state. Also, for every state $x$ and every $0<t<1$, the equal-state scaled split $(t x,(1-t)x)$ is reversible to $x$.

**T3 (thermal-equilibrium transitivity).** If $x\sim_T y$ and $y\sim_T z$ in the model’s declared contact family, then $x\sim_T z$. This requires the model to provide the relevant joined types and identifications.

**T4 (transversality).** For each simple-system state $x$, there are $x_0,x_1$ in that system with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$.

The axioms apply to admitted types and their joins only. T4 is an assumption about the contact relation; it is not a consequence of an equation of state or of a thermometer reading. The stronger range condition T5 is stated separately in [[post-td-universal-thermal-range]], and join coherence C1 is separately stated in [[post-td-equilibrium-join-coherence]].

For the simple-compressible physical branch, a primitive label is a pair $i=(c_i,n^i)$ of constitution and fixed positive mole amounts. Its numerical state domain is exactly $\Gamma_i=\Gamma_{c_i,n^i}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], with embedding $b_i(u,v)=(u,v,\hat n^i)\in D_{c_i}$. The unit map sends $(u,v)$ to $(u\,\mathrm J,v\,\mathrm{m^3})$; thus $u$ is the numerical value of the fixed internal energy, not a newly oriented energy coordinate. The underlying accessibility is the pullback of the admitted physical endpoint relation along $b_i$. Positive bulk scaling uses the declared scaling of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], carries the mole vector to $\lambda n^i$, and retains the distinct scaled tag. More general work coordinates or formal thermometer examples require their own explicitly declared domain, coordinate unit map and endpoint relation; no identification with $D_c$ is supplied by this definition.

For two named simple-system types $i,j$ with energy/work coordinates $x=(u_i,v_i)$ and $y=(u_j,v_j)$, a thermal join is the model-declared compound state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ whose energy coordinate is $u_i+u_j$ and whose work coordinates retain the ordered pair $(v_i,v_j)$. Its join domain consists exactly of those tuples $(u,v_i,v_j)$ for which there are $u_i,u_j$ with $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$ in the component domains and $u=u_i+u_j$. This is a tagged join state, distinct from the separated pair $(x,y)$, even when their total coordinates agree. The joined domain retains both work coordinates and has aggregate mole composition $n^i+n^j$ (in a common declared species list); it is not thereby a simple-compressible slice of one $D_c$. The contact model supplies its joined equilibrium endpoint space, endpoint coordinate map and admitted process relation. The contact model declares the pair encoding and join encoding to have the same aggregate composition and extends its accessibility relation to these two encodings; the contact axioms specify which such comparisons are admitted.

Write $x\sim_T y$ exactly when the pair $(x,y)$ and its join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ are accessible in both directions under the declared contact operation. Here $\sim_T$ is a relation between states of the two named systems; it is not numerical equality of temperature. Nested joins use only the model’s declared reassociation and permutation identifications. The coordinate sum alone supplies no accessibility comparison.

Adopt **T5 (universal thermal-equilibrium range)**: for every ordered pair of simple systems $i,j$, each state $x$ of $i$, and every work-coordinate point $v_j$ in the projection of the state domain of $j$, there is some state $y=(u_j,v_j)$ of $j$ with $x\sim_T y$, using [[def-td-thermal-join]].

This is a quantified existence assumption for a thermal-equilibrium partner at each permitted work coordinate. It does not define a numerical temperature, assert that all systems possess the same temperature range as a real apparatus, or supply a calibration map and its uncertainty.

Adopt **C1 (equilibrium-join coherence)**: whenever $x\sim_T y$, the joined state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ is thermally equivalent to each constituent, $J_{ij}(x,y)\sim_T x$ and $J_{ij}(x,y)\sim_T y$, using the model’s declared nested-join identifications.

C1 is an additional postulate of this completed contact branch. The source’s Theorem 4.8 is stated with T1–T4; the local conditional calibrator route uses the constituent-to-join bridge in addition to the stronger T5 range assumption. Neither fact licenses deriving C1 from $u=u_i+u_j$, from T1–T4, or from transitivity alone. The displayed source supports the contact context, not the claim that its bare printed axioms already contain C1.

Let $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ be simple domains in a family of finite thermal joins satisfying A1–A7, S1–S3, T1–T5, and C1 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]]. Then there are $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ in $\Gamma_1$ and $y_0\prec\prec y_1$ in $\Gamma_2$ such that

$$(x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0).$$

Moreover, for every fixed finite composition of scaled copies of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, any two equal-mass states of that same composition are comparable (CH). The conclusion is conditional on the explicitly stated join-coherence and universal-range assumptions C1 and T5.

Let $P$ be a set of primitive type labels. A formal type $\Gamma$ records a finitely supported amount function $\nu_\Gamma:P\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, not identically zero. Primitive generators have their unit amount function. Positive scaling, separated product, and thermal-join constructors retain distinct formal tags and obey

$$\nu_{s\Gamma}=s\nu_\Gamma,\qquad \nu_{\Gamma\otimes\Gamma'}=\nu_\Gamma+\nu_{\Gamma'}\qquad(s>0).$$

Separated and joined types are distinct constructors even when their amount functions agree. Permutation, reassociation, and scaled-splitting conventions preserve the amount function. Define the positive **bookkeeping weight** $w_\Gamma:=\sum_{p\in P}\nu_\Gamma(p)$, a finite sum over support. Thus $w_{s\Gamma}=s w_\Gamma$ and every product or join has weight $w_\Gamma+w_{\Gamma'}$. The optional empty unit has zero amount function and weight zero; it is represented only by the empty compound, not as a simple chart. These are formal amounts, not masses in kilograms or an empirical conservation law. The functions and pointwise operations use [[def-function-space]]; their finite-support convention and finite sums are those of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]].

Let $I$ index the declared family of simple types $\Gamma_i$. For each simple type $\Gamma$ in that family, let $n_\Gamma\ge1$ and let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n_\Gamma+1}$ be nonempty, open and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$. The notation for a type and its chart is shared, but each state has a distinct raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$. Scaled charts are distinct tagged copies $s\Gamma=\{sx:x\in\Gamma\}$ with coordinate transport $x\mapsto sx$; transported raw tags remain distinct from the original raw tags. Let $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$ be the unit point mass from [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. The represented state is

$$\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x):=w_\Gamma e_{(\Gamma,x)},\qquad m(\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))=w_\Gamma.$$

Write $\mathsf{J}(x):=\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ when $x$ already carries its type tag. All state notation in this framework's compound comparisons, including a bare $x$, denotes $\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$; a raw unit point mass is always written $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. A separated pair is addition of represented states, not a unit product tag. Nonnegative multiples are pointwise and zero terms are omitted. For an encoded compound $c$, its aggregate composition is the finite amount function

$$\nu(c):=\sum_{(\Gamma,x)\in\operatorname{supp}(c)}\frac{c(\Gamma,x)}{w_\Gamma}\nu_\Gamma;\qquad m(c)=\sum_{p\in P}\nu(c)(p).$$

Fix the formal interpretation $\Pi(c)$ as the finite separated preparation whose factor at each nonzero raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$ is the amount $c(\Gamma,x)/w_\Gamma$ of that typed state, using the declared coordinate scaling transport. The accessibility relation on coefficient maps is the pullback of the declared relation on these preparations. Merging or splitting repeated copies of the same preparation is reversible; permutation and reassociation preserve the preparation. Thus $\Pi(\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx))$ and $\Pi(s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))$ are the same declared scaled preparation and yield

$$\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx)\sim s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x),$$

although their raw point masses have different tags and are not equal. This reversible transport commutes with finite composition, nested type constructors, and scaled splitting. It is part of the precise formal scaling interpretation, not a deduction about physical accessibility from coordinate multiplication. A physical use must adopt the stated preparation maps and accessibility assumptions; fixed-composition models compare only preparations with the same $\nu$, while a declared channel model may additionally compare different compositions of equal $m$.

A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only when $m(A)=m(B)$, as in the coefficient-map supplier. Write $A\sim B$ when both directions hold, and $A\prec\prec B$ when only the forward direction holds. On any fixed simple type, dividing every represented state by the same positive constant $w_\Gamma$ gives its unit-point-mass comparison. Positive scaling and its inverse preserve and reflect order; whenever the required CH and reference hypotheses hold, the unit-state entropy theorem applies after that normalization. If $S$ represents unit-point-mass comparisons, the entropy of a represented state is $w_\Gamma S(x)$ and the entropy of a finite sum $\sum_j t_j\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x_j)$ is $\sum_j t_j w_\Gamma S(x_j)$. No independent rescaling across different types is assumed without a calibrator.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $t\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ is equivalent to $s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)+(t-s)\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ for $t>0$ and $0<s<t$, with the reversible scaled-copy transport above; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)\prec\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $x,y\in\Gamma_i$ and $0<t<1$, the encoded compound $t\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+(1-t)\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)$ compares to $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(tx+(1-t)y)$; both have bookkeeping mass $w_{\Gamma_i}$, and convexity puts the recombined coordinate in the chart; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with a finite-valued slope map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For every declared finite family of simple-system domains closed under the thermal joins of [[def-td-thermal-join]], assume the accessibility axioms A1–A6, the simple-system assumptions A7 and S1–S3, the contact assumptions T1–T4, the universal thermal-equilibrium range T5, and equilibrium-join coherence C1, with the exact formulations in [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], [[post-td-simple-system-geometric-axioms]], [[post-td-thermal-join-axioms]], [[post-td-universal-thermal-range]], and [[post-td-equilibrium-join-coherence]]. Then for any two simple types $i,j$, there are $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ in $i$ and $y_0\prec\prec y_1$ in $j$ such that

$$ (x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0). $$

Moreover, for this fixed pair $i,j$, every finite separated product made only from positive scaled copies of $i$ and $j$ satisfies the comparison hypothesis: any two equal-formal-mass states $A,B$ of that product type satisfy $A\prec B$ or $B\prec A$. No comparison conclusion for products involving a third primitive type is contained in this pairwise result. These are conditional model deductions. In particular, the conclusion is not claimed from the printed Theorem 4.8 interface with T1–T4 alone; the local mathematical supplier explicitly requires the additional T5 and C1 branch.

Let $I$ be a nonempty set of primitive simple-system labels containing a distinguished meter label $m$. Assume every finite separated product is explicitly represented by its finitely many tagged elementary factors; positive scaling and finite product are the only identifications. Suppose the join-closed family satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]], and fix a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then one can choose, for every $i\in I$, an additive constant and positive scale for its same-type entropy so that

$$S\big((t_1i_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_ni_n,x_n)\big)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$$

is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison on every finite separated product. No conclusion is asserted for transitions that change composition.

For each simple-system chart $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$, $n_i\ge1$, let $x=(u,v)$, with one energy coordinate $u$ and $n_i$ work coordinates $v$. The chart is a nonempty open convex domain. The simple-compressible physical case is the fixed-composition slice and embedding of [[def-td-thermal-join]], with $n_i=1$, $u=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $v=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$. A declared multi-work chart or joined chart instead supplies its own equilibrium endpoint domain and diagonal unit map: $U=u(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $W_a=v_a w_a$ for fixed positive work-coordinate units $w_a$. The numerical domain is identified with these physical endpoints by that supplied map, and accessibility is pulled back from the admitted endpoint relation. These identifications preserve the internal-energy meaning and fixed composition; extra work coordinates do not follow from the simple-compressible state definition. Adopt these assumptions for every state $x$ and for every thermal join treated as a simple system:

**A7 (convex-combination accessibility).** For $0<t<1$, the separated scaled pair $(t x,(1-t)y)$ is accessible to the chart state $t x+(1-t)y$, whenever these states are in the declared domains.

For each $x$, define its forward sector $A_x=\{y\in\Gamma_i:x\prec y\}$. Adopt:

**S1 (strict successor).** Some $y\in\Gamma_i$ satisfies $x\prec\prec y$.

**S2 (unique finite-slope support).** At $x=(u_x,v_x)$, $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane through $x$, and it can be written
$$
u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0
$$
with finite $P_i(x)\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$. The map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$ is locally Lipschitz: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite Lipschitz constant bounds $\|P_i(x)-P_i(y)\|/\|x-y\|$. A supporting hyperplane means $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets it at $x$.

**S3 (connected relative boundary).** The boundary $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$, taken in the topology relative to $\Gamma_i$, is arcwise connected.

These are explicit adopted conditions. The slope $P_i$ is a geometric support parameter here; no equation identifying it with measured pressure is asserted. In particular, S1–S3 and A7 do not assert comparison hypothesis for products.

Fix a family $I$ of primitive material labels. A tagged type $c\in I$ retains its identity even if another type has the same coordinate domain. A positive scale $\lambda>0$ is dimensionless and is represented by the separately tagged bulk copy $c^{(\lambda)}$ and map $\delta_\lambda$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A finite separated compound is a finite tuple of tagged scaled systems, with permutation and reassociation identifications and an empty unit type. Its state is a tuple of constituent equilibrium states; its extensive coordinate tuple is the sum specified by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] whenever the pair is admitted there.

The formal composition vector of a compound records, for each primitive label $c$, the sum of its positive scale coefficients. Two compounds have the same composition exactly when these vectors agree. The distinct **formal mass** $m(A)$ is the sum of all scale coefficients in $A$, a dimensionless bookkeeping quantity; it is not physical mass in kilograms, mole amount, energy, or volume. Same-composition compounds have equal formal mass. For states $A,B$ of the same compound type, write $A\prec B$ when the declared adiabatic-accessibility relation of [[def-td-adiabatic-accessibility]] admits that endpoint comparison. This definition does not infer accessibility from coordinate addition.

An equal-composition comparison is a comparison between states of types with the same formal composition vector. The later reaction-network definition may separately admit transitions between distinct composition types, but the mathematical supplier still requires equal formal mass at both endpoints. A physical application must state how its channel preserves the chosen formal mass and separately record its dimensioned conservation balances. The empty unit has one state and formal mass zero. No identity is imposed between a primitive type and a scaled tag, or between two different decompositions of a compound, beyond the explicitly declared reassociation, permutation, and bulk-composition maps.

derivations.claim: Fix a finite set of primitive labels from $I$. For every pair in this set, [A2] supplies a strict calibrator and comparison hypothesis on all finite products formed from that pair; the relation also satisfies the six accessibility assumptions of the physical model. These are the pairwise contact inputs required by [A3], not a claim that the pair theorem alone compares products involving three or more primitive types. The factors have the explicit tagged finite representation in [A5].

Since $I$ is nonempty, choose a primitive type $m$ as the distinguished meter label. Applying [A2] to the ordered pair $(m,m)$ supplies a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. For each $j\ne m$, applying [A2] to the ordered pair $(j,m)$ supplies states $a_j,b_j\in\Gamma_j$ and $c_j,d_j\in\Gamma_m$ with $a_j\prec\prec b_j$, $c_j\prec\prec d_j$, and $(a_j,d_j)\sim(b_j,c_j)$, exactly the calibrator orientation required by [A3]. Choice [A1] selects the reference states, same-type entropy representatives and calibrator data simultaneously across $I$, exactly as [A3] requires. Use the composition-preserving coefficient-map interpretation constructed in [A2]: each actual state is represented by its type-weighted point mass, and scalar amount $t$ has the encoded state value $t$ times that state entropy. In [A3], same-type unit-label representations are converted back to represented-state values by their positive type weights, so the calibration describes the original tagged preparations, not independently rescaled entropy units for joined types. Each compound contains only finitely many tagged factors. The empty unit has value zero as the empty entropy sum; every nonempty compound is a finite sum of tagged factor entropies. Applying [A3] gives a single function $\widetilde S$ on the family of all such finite compounds, additive on concatenation, homogeneous under each positive scale, and order-equivalent to $\prec$ for each equal-composition comparison. No infinite sum is introduced because every state has finite support.

Let $x,y$ lie in one simple chart and $0<t<1$. By [A4], the scaled pair $(t x,(1-t)y)$ compares to the recombined state $t x+(1-t)y$. The representation in step 2.1 turns that comparison into $$ t\widetilde S(x)+(1-t)\widetilde S(y)\le \widetilde S(t x+(1-t)y), $$ where additivity and extensivity evaluate the pair entropy. This is precisely concavity on the admitted convex chart; the endpoint weights $t=0,1$ give equality.

A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

Assume the calibrated entropy family of [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]], the cross-type accessibility axioms A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and the decorated cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. For every pair of types $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ and states $x\in X_\Gamma$, $y\in X_{\Gamma'}$,

$$x\prec y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_\Gamma(x)+F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y).$$

The infimum defining $F$ need not be attained. If $F=+\infty$, the right side is false; if $F=-\infty$, the right side is true.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $F$ be the decorated cost of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], and assume the **no-sinks condition**

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty$$

for every type pair. Let $V_F$ be the real difference space of [[def-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space]]. Then there is an additive extensive offset $B:\mathcal G\to\mathbb R$ such that

$$-F(\Gamma',\Gamma)\le B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma').$$

If every admitted cross-type transition $x\prec y$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ satisfies the calibrated cost inequality of [[thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-inference]], then $\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)$ is nondecreasing across every such transition. Only this weak inequality is asserted; no-gap equalities and strict extensions are not concluded.

derivations.claim: Fix an admitted transition $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$. The network’s no-sinks condition and [A1] match the hypotheses of [F4]; its cost is the same $F$ as in step 1.1 by [F2] and [F3]. The same $B$ works for every admitted transition, proving the conditional weak entropy principle.

For the simple-compressible physical branch, a primitive label is a pair $i=(c_i,n^i)$ of constitution and fixed positive mole amounts. Its numerical state domain is exactly $\Gamma_i=\Gamma_{c_i,n^i}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], with embedding $b_i(u,v)=(u,v,\hat n^i)\in D_{c_i}$. The unit map sends $(u,v)$ to $(u\,\mathrm J,v\,\mathrm{m^3})$; thus $u$ is the numerical value of the fixed internal energy, not a newly oriented energy coordinate. The underlying accessibility is the pullback of the admitted physical endpoint relation along $b_i$. Positive bulk scaling uses the declared scaling of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], carries the mole vector to $\lambda n^i$, and retains the distinct scaled tag. More general work coordinates or formal thermometer examples require their own explicitly declared domain, coordinate unit map and endpoint relation; no identification with $D_c$ is supplied by this definition.

For two named simple-system types $i,j$ with energy/work coordinates $x=(u_i,v_i)$ and $y=(u_j,v_j)$, a thermal join is the model-declared compound state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ whose energy coordinate is $u_i+u_j$ and whose work coordinates retain the ordered pair $(v_i,v_j)$. Its join domain consists exactly of those tuples $(u,v_i,v_j)$ for which there are $u_i,u_j$ with $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$ in the component domains and $u=u_i+u_j$. This is a tagged join state, distinct from the separated pair $(x,y)$, even when their total coordinates agree. The joined domain retains both work coordinates and has aggregate mole composition $n^i+n^j$ (in a common declared species list); it is not thereby a simple-compressible slice of one $D_c$. The contact model supplies its joined equilibrium endpoint space, endpoint coordinate map and admitted process relation. The contact model declares the pair encoding and join encoding to have the same aggregate composition and extends its accessibility relation to these two encodings; the contact axioms specify which such comparisons are admitted.

Write $x\sim_T y$ exactly when the pair $(x,y)$ and its join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ are accessible in both directions under the declared contact operation. Here $\sim_T$ is a relation between states of the two named systems; it is not numerical equality of temperature. Nested joins use only the model’s declared reassociation and permutation identifications. The coordinate sum alone supplies no accessibility comparison.

Adopt the following axioms for $\prec$ on every declared pair of finite compounds with equal formal mass in [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]. Initially this covers equal-composition adiabatic accessibility. If a later channel model admits comparisons between distinct composition types, the same axioms apply to those comparisons and all their finite scaled products; no cross-type transition is admitted by this postulate alone. They are assumptions of the operational model, not consequences of the process definition or of energy additivity.

**A1 (reflexivity).** $A\prec A$ for every state $A$.

**A2 (transitivity).** If $A\prec B$ and $B\prec C$, then $A\prec C$.

**A3 (consistency).** If $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every finite spectator compound $C$ for which both endpoint compounds are admitted and the resulting formal masses agree.

**A4 (scaling).** If $A\prec B$, then $\lambda A\prec\lambda B$ for every $\lambda>0$, using the tagged scaling maps of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]].

**A5 (splitting).** For each state $x$, positive $s<t$, and tagged scaled copies of its material, the state $t x$ is accessible in both directions to the separated pair $(s x,(t-s)x)$. This states reversible splitting of an equilibrium preparation into scaled copies, not additivity of arbitrary state functions.

**A6 (stability).** Let $A,B$ have equal formal mass. Let $Z_0,Z_1$ be fixed positive spectator compounds of equal formal mass, and let $\epsilon_n>0$ decrease to zero. If $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for every $n$, then $A\prec B$.

Equality of formal masses in A6 is required so each comparison is defined; equality of composition vectors is not required when a declared model includes cross-type transitions. A6 is a limiting closure assumption on the relation; it does not assert continuity of any physical process or the existence of a limiting apparatus.

For each simple-system chart $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$, $n_i\ge1$, let $x=(u,v)$, with one energy coordinate $u$ and $n_i$ work coordinates $v$. The chart is a nonempty open convex domain. The simple-compressible physical case is the fixed-composition slice and embedding of [[def-td-thermal-join]], with $n_i=1$, $u=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $v=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$. A declared multi-work chart or joined chart instead supplies its own equilibrium endpoint domain and diagonal unit map: $U=u(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $W_a=v_a w_a$ for fixed positive work-coordinate units $w_a$. The numerical domain is identified with these physical endpoints by that supplied map, and accessibility is pulled back from the admitted endpoint relation. These identifications preserve the internal-energy meaning and fixed composition; extra work coordinates do not follow from the simple-compressible state definition. Adopt these assumptions for every state $x$ and for every thermal join treated as a simple system:

**A7 (convex-combination accessibility).** For $0<t<1$, the separated scaled pair $(t x,(1-t)y)$ is accessible to the chart state $t x+(1-t)y$, whenever these states are in the declared domains.

For each $x$, define its forward sector $A_x=\{y\in\Gamma_i:x\prec y\}$. Adopt:

**S1 (strict successor).** Some $y\in\Gamma_i$ satisfies $x\prec\prec y$.

**S2 (unique finite-slope support).** At $x=(u_x,v_x)$, $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane through $x$, and it can be written
$$
u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0
$$
with finite $P_i(x)\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$. The map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$ is locally Lipschitz: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite Lipschitz constant bounds $\|P_i(x)-P_i(y)\|/\|x-y\|$. A supporting hyperplane means $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets it at $x$.

**S3 (connected relative boundary).** The boundary $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$, taken in the topology relative to $\Gamma_i$, is arcwise connected.

These are explicit adopted conditions. The slope $P_i$ is a geometric support parameter here; no equation identifying it with measured pressure is asserted. In particular, S1–S3 and A7 do not assert comparison hypothesis for products.

Use thermal joins and $\sim_T$ exactly as defined in [[def-td-thermal-join]]. For every ordered pair of simple systems and every admitted finite join, adopt:

**T1 (joining).** $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$.

**T2 (reversible splitting).** Every join state has at least one split into component states at its stated total energy and work coordinates that is reversible to the join state. Also, for every state $x$ and every $0<t<1$, the equal-state scaled split $(t x,(1-t)x)$ is reversible to $x$.

**T3 (thermal-equilibrium transitivity).** If $x\sim_T y$ and $y\sim_T z$ in the model’s declared contact family, then $x\sim_T z$. This requires the model to provide the relevant joined types and identifications.

**T4 (transversality).** For each simple-system state $x$, there are $x_0,x_1$ in that system with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$.

The axioms apply to admitted types and their joins only. T4 is an assumption about the contact relation; it is not a consequence of an equation of state or of a thermometer reading. The stronger range condition T5 is stated separately in [[post-td-universal-thermal-range]], and join coherence C1 is separately stated in [[post-td-equilibrium-join-coherence]].

Adopt **T5 (universal thermal-equilibrium range)**: for every ordered pair of simple systems $i,j$, each state $x$ of $i$, and every work-coordinate point $v_j$ in the projection of the state domain of $j$, there is some state $y=(u_j,v_j)$ of $j$ with $x\sim_T y$, using [[def-td-thermal-join]].

This is a quantified existence assumption for a thermal-equilibrium partner at each permitted work coordinate. It does not define a numerical temperature, assert that all systems possess the same temperature range as a real apparatus, or supply a calibration map and its uncertainty.

Adopt **C1 (equilibrium-join coherence)**: whenever $x\sim_T y$, the joined state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ is thermally equivalent to each constituent, $J_{ij}(x,y)\sim_T x$ and $J_{ij}(x,y)\sim_T y$, using the model’s declared nested-join identifications.

C1 is an additional postulate of this completed contact branch. The source’s Theorem 4.8 is stated with T1–T4; the local conditional calibrator route uses the constituent-to-join bridge in addition to the stronger T5 range assumption. Neither fact licenses deriving C1 from $u=u_i+u_j$, from T1–T4, or from transitivity alone. The displayed source supports the contact context, not the claim that its bare printed axioms already contain C1.

For all $x,y\in\mathbb R$ and $0\le t\le1$,
$$\exp((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)\exp x+t\exp y.$$
If $0<t<1$, equality holds exactly when $x=y$.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

For $a>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$a^x:=\exp(x\log a).$$
For the supplementary zero-base convention, define $0^x:=0$ when $x>0$.

The expressions $0^0$ and $0^x$ for $x<0$ are left undefined. Negative bases are not assigned arbitrary real powers.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

derivations.claim: For $a,b>0$, apply [F6] to $\log a,\log b$, then use [F7] and monotonicity of $\log$, to obtain $\log((1-t)a+tb)\ge(1-t)\log a+t\log b$ for $0\le t\le1$. Apply this inequality to the energy ratios $u/u_{\star,i}$ and to the work ratios $v/v_{\star,i}$; multiplying by $c_i,r_i>0$ and adding $b_i$ proves concavity of $s_i$. This verifies the convex-combination accessibility condition. Since $\log$ is strictly increasing, raising $u$ at fixed $v$ gives a strict successor, proving S1.

The boundary equation $s_i(u',v')=s_i(u_x,v_x)$ rearranges to $u'=g(v')=K(v')^{-\alpha}$, where $K=u_xv_x^\alpha>0$ and $\alpha=r_i/c_i>0$. By [F8], $g'=-\alpha K(v')^{-\alpha-1}$ and $g''=\alpha(\alpha+1)K(v')^{-\alpha-2}>0$. Thus $g'$ is increasing by [F9]. For $v'\ne v_x$, the mean value theorem on the interval between them and the monotonicity of $g'$ give $g(v')\ge g(v_x)+g'(v_x)(v'-v_x)$: when $v'<v_x$, both the derivative comparison and the sign of $v'-v_x$ reverse. Hence the forward sector $u'\ge g(v')$ lies above the tangent support $u'-u_x+(r_i u_x/(c_iv_x))(v'-v_x)=0$. A vertical line cannot support this sector because its work coordinate varies on both sides at an interior boundary point. If a nonvertical line with slope parameter $q$ supports there, its inequality on graph points gives $g(v')-g(v_x)+q(v'-v_x)\ge0$ for both signs of $v'-v_x$; dividing by that difference and taking limits forces $q=-g'(v_x)$. This proves uniqueness and gives $P_i=r_i u_x/(c_iv_x)$. On any closed rectangle with $u,\tilde u\le u_1$ and $v,\tilde v\ge v_0>0$, $|u/v-\tilde u/\tilde v|\le |u-\tilde u|/v_0+u_1|v-\tilde v|/v_0^2$, so the slope is locally Lipschitz. The graph over $v'>0$ is arcwise connected, proving S3.

Put $C=c_i+c_j$. For any split $u_i+u_j=u$, [F6] with weights $c_i/C,c_j/C$, followed by [F7], gives $$\frac{c_i}{C}\log\frac{u_i}{c_i}+\frac{c_j}{C}\log\frac{u_j}{c_j}\le\log\frac{u}{C},$$ with equality exactly when $u_i/c_i=u_j/c_j$. Since $u_i+u_j=u$, that equality forces the unique split $u_i=c_i u/C,\ u_j=c_j u/C$. Multiply by $C$ and add the constants $c_i\log(c_i/u_{\star,i})+c_j\log(c_j/u_{\star,j})+b_i+b_j+r_i\log(v_i/v_{\star,i})+r_j\log(v_j/v_{\star,j})$; the resulting inequality is exactly the pair entropy bounded by its value at that split. By the declared total-entropy comparison, this proves T1 and shows that the maximizing split is reversible with the join, establishing the join-splitting clause of T2. For the equal-state scaled split, tagged extensivity gives $s_{ti}(tu,tv)=t s_i(u,v)$ and $s_{(1-t)i}((1-t)u,(1-t)v)=(1-t)s_i(u,v)$, so both sides have equal entropy and the other T2 clause holds. The binary join entropy is $C\log u+r_i\log v_i+r_j\log v_j+C_{ij}$ for a constant $C_{ij}$; its energy-to-coefficient ratio is $u/C=u_i/c_i=u_j/c_j$ at the maximizing split.

By the declared total-entropy comparison, every finite product has a real-valued order. Reflexivity and transitivity follow from the real order; adding the same spectator adds the same number to both sides; positive scaling multiplies the sums by a positive coefficient; and reversible splitting preserves the extensive sum. If $A+\epsilon_nZ_0\prec B+\epsilon_nZ_1$, then $s(A)-s(B)\le\epsilon_n(s(Z_1)-s(Z_0))$. Taking $n\to\infty$ yields $s(A)\le s(B)$ and hence $A\prec B$. This verifies the six adopted order conditions.

For a single system the entropy has the displayed logarithmic form. If a nested join has energy coefficient $C$ and is joined with a system of coefficient $c>0$, the maximum calculation of step 1.3 gives the unique maximizing split at equal energy-to-coefficient ratios; substitution adds $c$ to the energy coefficient and adds the new work term. Induction over the finite joins therefore gives coefficient $C=\sum_k c_k$ and entropy $C\log u+\sum_k r_k\log v_k+C_0$ for the positive work coordinates $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)$. Its boundary is $u=g(v)=K\prod_k v_k^{-\alpha_k}$ with $\alpha_k=r_k/C>0$. Direct differentiation gives, for any vector $h$, $$D^2g(v)[h,h]=g(v)\left[\left(\sum_k\alpha_k\frac{h_k}{v_k}\right)^2+\sum_k\alpha_k\left(\frac{h_k}{v_k}\right)^2\right]\ge0.$$ Thus along each segment in the positive work orthant, the derivative of $g$ is nondecreasing by [F9], and the mean value theorem gives $g(v')\ge g(v)+\nabla g(v)\cdot(v'-v)$. The forward sector $u\ge g(v)$ lies above this tangent support; uniqueness follows by applying the support inequality to graph points in each direction $h$ and $-h$, which forces the support functional to equal $\nabla g(v)$. Its finite slope components are $P_k=r_k u/(Cv_k)$; on rectangles bounded away from all coordinate axes, the quotient estimate from step 1.2 applies to each component and proves local Lipschitz regularity. The positive orthant and its graph are arcwise connected. Increasing $u$ gives S1, and the coordinatewise concavity argument of step 1.1 gives the convex-combination accessibility condition. Hence each join satisfies the same simple-system geometry.

Applying the two-weight maximum calculation of steps 1.3 and 2.2 to any two primitive or recursively joined types $A,B$ shows that $x=(u_A,v_A)$ and $y=(u_B,v_B)$ are thermally equivalent exactly when $u_A/C_A=u_B/C_B$, where $C_A,C_B>0$ are their energy coefficients. Equality of ratios is transitive, proving T3. For any such simple type with coefficient $C$ and at least one work coordinate $v_k$, fix a state $x=(u,v)$ and choose $0<v_k^-<v_k<v_k^+$, keeping $u$ and all other coordinates fixed. The entropy formula of step 2.2 strictly increases with $v_k$, so $x_-\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_+$. Both outer states have the same ratio $u/C$ and hence are thermally equivalent. This proves T4 for primitive and recursively joined simple types.

Let $A,B$ be any primitive or recursively joined simple types, with energy coefficients $C_A,C_B>0$. Given $x=(u_A,v_A)$ and any allowed work-coordinate vector $v_B$, choose $u_B=C_Bu_A/C_A$. The two-weight maximum calculation in steps 1.3 and 2.2 makes $x$ thermally equivalent to $y=(u_B,v_B)$, proving T5. For any equilibrated pair $x,y$, the same calculation gives $u_A/C_A=u_B/C_B$. Their joined state has energy coefficient $C_A+C_B$ and energy $u_A+u_B$, so its ratio equals the common ratio; the two-weight maximum criterion therefore makes that joined state thermally equivalent to $x$, and likewise to $y$. This proves C1 for every admitted join.

citations.quote:
Fix a family $I$ of primitive material labels. A tagged type $c\in I$ retains its identity even if another type has the same coordinate domain. A positive scale $\lambda>0$ is dimensionless and is represented by the separately tagged bulk copy $c^{(\lambda)}$ and map $\delta_\lambda$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A finite separated compound is a finite tuple of tagged scaled systems, with permutation and reassociation identifications and an empty unit type. Its state is a tuple of constituent equilibrium states; its extensive coordinate tuple is the sum specified by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] whenever the pair is admitted there.

The formal composition vector of a compound records, for each primitive label $c$, the sum of its positive scale coefficients. Two compounds have the same composition exactly when these vectors agree. The distinct **formal mass** $m(A)$ is the sum of all scale coefficients in $A$, a dimensionless bookkeeping quantity; it is not physical mass in kilograms, mole amount, energy, or volume. Same-composition compounds have equal formal mass. For states $A,B$ of the same compound type, write $A\prec B$ when the declared adiabatic-accessibility relation of [[def-td-adiabatic-accessibility]] admits that endpoint comparison. This definition does not infer accessibility from coordinate addition.

An equal-composition comparison is a comparison between states of types with the same formal composition vector. The later reaction-network definition may separately admit transitions between distinct composition types, but the mathematical supplier still requires equal formal mass at both endpoints. A physical application must state how its channel preserves the chosen formal mass and separately record its dimensioned conservation balances. The empty unit has one state and formal mass zero. No identity is imposed between a primitive type and a scaled tag, or between two different decompositions of a compound, beyond the explicitly declared reassociation, permutation, and bulk-composition maps.

Use thermal joins and $\sim_T$ exactly as defined in [[def-td-thermal-join]]. For every ordered pair of simple systems and every admitted finite join, adopt:

**T1 (joining).** $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$.

**T2 (reversible splitting).** Every join state has at least one split into component states at its stated total energy and work coordinates that is reversible to the join state. Also, for every state $x$ and every $0<t<1$, the equal-state scaled split $(t x,(1-t)x)$ is reversible to $x$.

**T3 (thermal-equilibrium transitivity).** If $x\sim_T y$ and $y\sim_T z$ in the model’s declared contact family, then $x\sim_T z$. This requires the model to provide the relevant joined types and identifications.

**T4 (transversality).** For each simple-system state $x$, there are $x_0,x_1$ in that system with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$.

The axioms apply to admitted types and their joins only. T4 is an assumption about the contact relation; it is not a consequence of an equation of state or of a thermometer reading. The stronger range condition T5 is stated separately in [[post-td-universal-thermal-range]], and join coherence C1 is separately stated in [[post-td-equilibrium-join-coherence]].

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

derivations.claim: Start at $(1,3)$. Then $\bar U=2$, every point of $A$ has second coordinate at least $3$, and every point of $B$ has second coordinate at least $2$. A finite convex combination of points whose second coordinates are at least $2$ still has second coordinate at least $2$, because it is the weighted sum of those coordinates with nonnegative weights summing to one. Hence every point in $\operatorname{conv}(A\cup B)$ has second coordinate at least $2$, so $(3,1)$ is not in the forward sector and $(1,3)\not\prec(3,1)$.

In the one-system space, strict accessibility is exactly strict increase of $U$, while thermal equilibrium is equality of normalized energies. If $U_0\prec\prec U\prec\prec U_1$, then $U_0<U<U_1$, so $U_0\ne U_1$ and the two cannot be thermally equivalent. Thus T4 fails.

Start instead at $(3,1)$. Again $\bar U=2$; every point of its $A$ has first coordinate at least $3$, and every point of its $B$ has first coordinate at least $2$. Convex combinations therefore have first coordinate at least $2$, so $(1,3)$ is not accessible from $(3,1)$. The two product states are incomparable, and the comparison hypothesis fails.

By [F4], $U$ is dimensionless, so the single-system function $S(U)=\log U$ is well-defined; it is strictly increasing and represents $U\le U'$. If its additive sum represented product accessibility, the states $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$ would have equal summed entropy $\log 3$, forcing accessibility both ways. Step 1.1 and step 2.1 show neither direction holds. Therefore this single-system entropy does not represent the product relation. Since the example fails T4 by step 1.2, it does not satisfy the hypotheses of a product-comparison result that includes T4.

definition_review.statement:
A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.
edge_cases: An empty channel set is permitted; no witness gives +infinity and unbounded-below costs give -infinity.
Equal endpoint composition types recover the fixed-composition process record; cross-type edges still require declared channel records and equal formal mass.
No-sinks is an explicit directed-pair equivalence required of an adopted network, not inferred from composition or proved as an empirical law.
definition_review.well_definedness: The Definition assigns the relation exactly by existence of admitted records with the stated endpoints. Finite decorated chains use those exact edges and real baseline-entropy costs; their infimum has the explicit +infinity/-infinity conventions. Accessibility A1–A6, conservation constraints and no-sinks are adopted model conditions.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed entire Definition and exact process-record, finite-compound, forward-encoding and decorated-cost suppliers. Channel tuple specifies endpoint domains/maps, finite seconds interval, arbitrary configuration path and protocol/boundary/transfer sets; admitted subset and balance predicate are model inputs, not derived conservation laws or guaranteed realizability. Energy/heat/work maps are J-valued and species maps mol-valued; formal amount/weight is explicitly separate. Network relation is exactly existential admitted-record reachability on equal-formal-mass endpoints and is the same relation in each chain edge. Finite-factor closure/A1-A6 are explicit further conditions; an empty raw channel family does not by itself satisfy reflexivity for nonempty states. Decorated costs require the supplier baseline entropy and common catalyst, N>=1 with finite real edge sums; unmatched masses have no witness. Infimum distinguishes missing witnesses (+infinity), unbounded costs (-infinity), and finite costs without pretending attainment. No-sinks is a required symmetric-reachability property, not a theorem or material assertion. No undefined subtraction of extended-real costs, hidden regularity or empirical premise. No local defect found.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
For the simple-compressible physical branch, a primitive label is a pair $i=(c_i,n^i)$ of constitution and fixed positive mole amounts. Its numerical state domain is exactly $\Gamma_i=\Gamma_{c_i,n^i}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], with embedding $b_i(u,v)=(u,v,\hat n^i)\in D_{c_i}$. The unit map sends $(u,v)$ to $(u\,\mathrm J,v\,\mathrm{m^3})$; thus $u$ is the numerical value of the fixed internal energy, not a newly oriented energy coordinate. The underlying accessibility is the pullback of the admitted physical endpoint relation along $b_i$. Positive bulk scaling uses the declared scaling of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], carries the mole vector to $\lambda n^i$, and retains the distinct scaled tag. More general work coordinates or formal thermometer examples require their own explicitly declared domain, coordinate unit map and endpoint relation; no identification with $D_c$ is supplied by this definition.

For two named simple-system types $i,j$ with energy/work coordinates $x=(u_i,v_i)$ and $y=(u_j,v_j)$, a thermal join is the model-declared compound state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ whose energy coordinate is $u_i+u_j$ and whose work coordinates retain the ordered pair $(v_i,v_j)$. Its join domain consists exactly of those tuples $(u,v_i,v_j)$ for which there are $u_i,u_j$ with $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$ in the component domains and $u=u_i+u_j$. This is a tagged join state, distinct from the separated pair $(x,y)$, even when their total coordinates agree. The joined domain retains both work coordinates and has aggregate mole composition $n^i+n^j$ (in a common declared species list); it is not thereby a simple-compressible slice of one $D_c$. The contact model supplies its joined equilibrium endpoint space, endpoint coordinate map and admitted process relation. The contact model declares the pair encoding and join encoding to have the same aggregate composition and extends its accessibility relation to these two encodings; the contact axioms specify which such comparisons are admitted.

Write $x\sim_T y$ exactly when the pair $(x,y)$ and its join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ are accessible in both directions under the declared contact operation. Here $\sim_T$ is a relation between states of the two named systems; it is not numerical equality of temperature. Nested joins use only the model’s declared reassociation and permutation identifications. The coordinate sum alone supplies no accessibility comparison.

Fix a system $s$ as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. A material constitution $c$ specifies a finite ordered list of named species $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$, with $r\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $r\ge1$, and the model parameters that identify the material. An equilibrium-preparation label in the set $E_c$ selects a single macrostate that the model designates as an equilibrium state for constitution $c$. The equilibrium designation is primitive model input here; it is not a dynamical equilibration theorem or a global-stability claim. For each admitted preparation, its mechanical model supplies a positive total mass and a defined center-of-mass velocity as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], so the allowed boost can select a center-of-mass rest chart in which its internal energy is recorded. A preparation for which these mechanical data are unavailable lies outside this framework. A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function-space]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.
